title: switching prerelease tokens
issue_text:
I call next_version("prerelease", prerelease_token=...) to move a version onto a different prerelease token. When the new token sorts before the current one, I get back a version lower than the one I started with, even though the docstring says next_version preserves natural order.

```
>>> from semver import Version
>>> v = Version.parse("4.5.6-rc.2")
>>> n = v.next_version("prerelease", prerelease_token="beta")
>>> n
Version(major=4, minor=5, patch=6, prerelease='beta.1', build=None)
>>> n > v
False
```

The same thing happens going from beta to alpha, or from rc to dev. Moving to a token that sorts later, such as dev to rc, is fine.

I expected next_version never to go backwards: the result should always be greater than the version it was called on. If restarting the new token on the same release would not give a higher version, it should move to the next patch and start the token there instead of raising an error, so the example above gives 4.5.7-beta.1.
